labels.label: T-abs-chronal-neighbours-tarentin/1-edge
labels.notes: I checked the statements against the compiled definitions (#print in a /tmp probe importing Causal.ChronalNeighbourBridge). ChronalNeighbours is ChronalPastNeighbours C and ChronalPastNeighbours C.dual, chronology taken in each open V (Causal/LadderLocal.lean:158, :163). Tarentin is: for all x, for all U in nhds x, there exist p in U and q in U with x in openDiamond top p q (Causal/Properties.lean:116). openDiamond U p q is interior (Jminus U {q} inter Jplus U {p}) (:77, :80). The elaborated signature of Causal.Causality.ChronalNeighbours.tarentin is {M} [TopologicalSpace M] {C : Causality M}, C.ChronalNeighbours -> C.Tarentin. That is the edge chronal_neighbours => tarentin with no extra premise, no separation axiom and no countability, using the library's definitions exactly. It is not vacuous: timelikeLine_chronalNeighbours (Causal/LadderLocal.lean:463). ChronalNeighbours.exists_lt_lt is the keeper's [[open]] argument as stated (programme/ladder.toml:2370). It gives an open V inside N, a and b in V with a <<_V x <<_V b, and I+_V(a) inter I-_V(b) a neighbourhood of x contained in diamond top a b. The docstring's 'namely interior N' is the proof's choice. The statement is existential, which is the argument's content. not_chronalNeighbours_of_not_tarentin is the contrapositive. Strictness of the edge comes from lightlikeLine_separates_Z (tarentin, no chronal neighbours), already recorded at programme/ladder.toml:919-922. The REPORT's checklist row 'separation, countability: weakened, none used' is true.

labels.label: T-abs-chronal-neighbours-tarentin/2-strongly-tarentin
labels.notes: tarentin_of_Zplus_Zminus has the signature C.Zplus = univ -> C.Zminus = univ -> C.Tarentin, with Zplus and Zminus the library's (Causal/Properties.lean:137, :140; def:strongly_tarentin_point, ETT.tex:774-778, quoted verbatim). Its pointwise form is exists_lt_lt_of_mem_Zplus_of_mem_Zminus. Iplus_inter_Iminus_subset_openDiamond (I+_U(p) inter I-_U(q) is a subset of openDiamond U p q, for every U) and mem_openDiamond_of_lt_of_lt are what their names say. 'Strictly weaker than chronal neighbours' is correct. The forward direction is the library's ChronalNeighbours.mem_Zplus and ChronalPastNeighbours.mem_Zminus (Causal/LadderLocal.lean:306, :313). For strictness, globalLine_separates_Z conjoins Zplus = univ, Zminus = univ, Tarentin and not ChronalNeighbours. The globalLine witnesses use mem_nhds_iff_exists_Ioo_subset and no metric. The reading caveat is right. AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalNeighbours_iff_Z ([T1Space M], Causal/ChronalNeighbourBridge.lean:196) makes the two hypotheses equal under absolute minimality, so on ETT's T2 spacetimes they coincide in the gluing reading (OQ-18, registers/DECISIONS.md:174). globalLine is not absolutely minimal, so it separates them only without gluing. lightlikeLine_separates_Z (GH, push-up, causally open, causally arc-connected, tarentin, Zplus = Zminus = empty, not ChronalNeighbours) holds in either reading, as claimed, because causally arc-connected implies absolutely minimal. Its Tarentin conjunct is timelikeLine_tarentin (Causal/Lines.lean:177) through definitional equality: the two lines have the same le, and openDiamond reads only le. The kernel accepts this, and the proof stays in the ETT layer. Layer-1 rule: the premises Zplus = univ and Zminus = univ are not ladder nodes and not in the target's uses. They are the paper's def:strongly_tarentin_point, defined in Causal/Properties.lean, and each is a neighbourhood condition on chronology at each point. I read them as an explicit localisation hypothesis. The closer discloses that the premise has no ladder node (for_keeper.implies[0].note). The paper remarks (rem:lorentz_tarentin ETT.tex:783-784, rem:tarentin_exemples ETT.tex:688-689, defi:causal_E0 ETT.tex:1349-1350, rem:sing_tarentin ETT.tex:1364-1365) say what the REPORT says. None is claimed to be wrong, and none is marked.

labels.label: T-abs-chronal-neighbours-tarentin/3-separations
labels.notes: isolatedLine_separates_chronalNeighbours_tarentin conjoins CausallyArcConnected, CausallyPlain, not Tarentin and not ChronalNeighbours. It takes the first three from tarentin_and_plain_needed.2.1, whose compiled type I printed (Causal/LocateExtension.lean:687), and the last through the new contrapositive. Every conjunct is the ladder's Lean name for causally_arc_connected, causally_plain, tarentin and chronal_neighbours. It holds in either reading, because the line is causally arc-connected. globalLine_separates_tarentin conjoins Tarentin, PushUp, CausallyOpen, IsCausal, not ChronalNeighbours and not AbsolutelyMinimal. globalLine.AbsolutelyMinimal elaborates to Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal, since Causal.Causality.AbsolutelyMinimal does not exist; that is the ladder's absolutely_minimal. Every other conjunct is the ladder's definition: Tarentin, PushUp, CausallyOpen (two-sided, DEC-8) and IsCausal. The space is R, T2 and second countable, so no `space` field is needed. The reading claim is right: the line is not absolutely minimal, so the result holds without gluing only (kb/0014, kb/0073, OQ-18, OQ-67 (b)). The docstring SCOPE states this correctly. The REPORT's finding for this label contains one wrong sentence (finding 1).

findings.what: 'An absolutely minimal witness would still be needed for the gluing reading' is asserted of both pairs. For tarentin -> absolutely_minimal it is incoherent. In the gluing reading of defi:causalite every causality is absolutely minimal (OQ-18, registers/DECISIONS.md:174), so tarentin => absolutely_minimal holds trivially there and no witness can exist: an absolutely minimal witness of 'not absolutely minimal' is a contradiction. The sentence is meaningful only for tarentin -> causally_arc_connected, which in the gluing reading wants an absolutely minimal, tarentin, non-causally-arc-connected causality. If the keeper or an OQ row copied the sentence, it would point the next planner at an impossible target. The Lean, the docstring SCOPE (lines 78-80) and for_keeper.open_settled are correct.
findings.fix: When recording, say this instead. In the gluing reading, tarentin => absolutely_minimal is trivially true. tarentin -> causally_arc_connected still wants an absolutely minimal witness that is tarentin and not causally arc-connected. Both pairs are settled false by Causal.globalLine_separates_tarentin in the reading without gluing.
